in the month Nisannu, at (its) end(?), you catch a male partridge
You pluck its wings, strangle it and flatten(?) it
you sprinkle salt (on it) and dry (it)
You crush (it) together with seed of the mountain GÍR.ḪAB-thorn
give it to him to drink in beer, and that man will have potency
you cut off its head and let its blood fall into water
that water you leave overnight under the stars
When the sun comes up you give it to him to drink
you wrap (it) in wool from the thigh(?) of a sheep
you smear it with salt (and) the nīnû-plant (Ú.KUR.RA), dry (it) and crush (it)
You mix (it) with flour of roasted grain and give it to him to drink
these 14 plants(?) you crush(?) together, mix with coarse flour and form into pel[lets]
with water (and) the k[asû-plant] you rin[se] his whole body
with p[ure] oil you anoint him repeatedly
Sumerian incantation, fragmentary and not understood in detail
the sinews and the intestines you crush with (lit. in) stones and decoct (them)
